title: SpaceX Stock (SPCX) Rises 0.1% to $139.94 (Nov 12)
summary: SpaceX stock (SPCX) rose 0.14% to $139.94 on Nov 12 as Bloomberg reported SpaceX and Tesla could announce a merger as soon as December.
body_markdown:
At the close, SPCX stood 37.98% below its 52-week high of $225.64 and 33.49% above its 52-week low of $104.83. It also finished above its June[IPO](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-an-ipo/) price of $135, as Stocktwits noted.


## Why SpaceX Stock Rose


Financial media tied the session's swing to new merger reporting, not to a SpaceX announcement. On Thursday, Bloomberg reported that SpaceX and Tesla could announce a combination as soon as December, with boards and advisers on both sides discussing price, control and how many SpaceX shares Tesla investors would receive, as reported by[Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/11/12/spacex-tesla-merger-announcement-december-report/) . Neither company commented, Electrek noted.


Covering the same report,[Stocktwits](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/tsla-stock-climbs-amid-reports-220701075.html) said SPCX rallied during the session before closing flat. People familiar with the talks said a key issue is separating Tesla's China manufacturing operations from SpaceX's U.S. government and defense contracts, and the companies have also considered an announcement slipping into early 2027, according to Stocktwits.


The talks build on Musk's October comments that both boards had formed special committees of independent directors to evaluate a combination. Musk said there is "no guarantee" of a deal and that he is not part of the discussions, per Stocktwits.


A day earlier, on November 11, Musk wrote on X that "it takes us ~2 months working 24/7 to get a large compute cluster working reliably" and guessed "closer to 6 months for others," according to[TIKR](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/musk-spacex-makes-compute-actually-222029068.html) , which noted that the rival comparison rests on Musk's own guess.


## SPCX Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Merger talks have moved to terms: per Electrek, boards and advisers are now working through price and control. Musk has cited possible cooperation in superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab semiconductor project, robotics and mass-to-orbit capabilities tied to Starlink, according to Stocktwits.
- Revenue guidance: SpaceX has guided first-quarter revenue to $33 billion to $37 billion, according to TIKR.


### Risks


- No agreement yet: neither company commented on the Bloomberg report, Musk has said there is "no guarantee" of a deal, and any announcement could slip into early 2027.
- Regulatory and political hurdles: ring-fencing Tesla's China operations is a main obstacle, and Democrats, who won control of Congress in the midterms, have said Musk's companies and political ties will get scrutiny, per Electrek.
- Heavy spending: TIKR puts SpaceX's trailing-twelve-month capital spending at $55.1 billion and free cash flow at negative $39.3 billion, and says the next quarterly results will show whether rental income keeps pace with that spending.
